description: Agents ship change-sets of hundreds of files every day across many repositories while reviewer attention stays fixed
naive_change: Rank flow-groups with an explicit read order and reserve deep dives for anchors where evidence flags risk Agent operators should split change-sets and cap daily volume per reviewer; diffcore only helps triage what still arrives.
outcomes: reviewer reaches a verdict on a large change-set without reading every hunk

description: Reviewers lose access to frontier models through pricing shifts, provider exits, or security policy such as air gaps
naive_change: Core analysis derives evidence without any model call; agents participate only optionally over MCP
outcomes: diffcore produces evidence for a change-set without any model

description: Projects are increasingly written by unattended agent loops with weak judgement, and their declared boundaries erode without anyone noticing
naive_change: Check each change-set against the boundaries the project already enforces with its own tooling and show each crossing on the graph A human owner must still approve boundary declarations and ratified rules; diffcore only makes erosion visible.
outcomes: reviewer sees each boundary a change-set crosses

description: Developers use different agents, test runners, profilers, linters, and hosts than diffcore authors, and those tools churn
naive_change: A provider boundary: every external tool reaches diffcore through one plugin contract and the core depends on none of them
outcomes: diffcore keeps working when a developer swaps a tool behind a provider

description: A contributor, compromised dependency, or scraped repository plants comments, docstrings, and commit messages written as instructions to any AI agent reading the code; reviewers point their own agents at untrusted repositories and that text reaches the agents verbatim through diffcore context and MCP payloads
naive_change: Tag every repository-originated string with an untrusted-origin marker in every MCP and HTTP payload, render it fenced, and require reviewer confirmation before an agent session on an untrusted project posts, accepts, or ratifies claims
outcomes: agent receives each repository-originated text span labelled as untrusted code content | reviewer sees which claims were posted from a session that read untrusted code

description: A team runs an implementing agent, another vendor's reviewing agent, and a security agent on one change-set; they post confident, conflicting claims on the same anchors and the reviewer trusts whichever is read first or ignores them all
naive_change: Record agent identity, role, and stance (asserts, disputes, qualifies) on every claim; render all claims on an anchor together with disputes paired beside the bearing evidence
outcomes: reviewer sees every dispute between agent claims on the same anchor | claim carries the identity and role of the agent that posted it

description: Agents tuned on reviewer approval learn to phrase claims evidence can never contradict, narrow, tautological, or covering only easy entities, so every claim checks out while checked coverage of the risky code falls
naive_change: Classify each claim's scope and whether it states a checkable predicate; show per change-set which changed entities no checkable claim covers so silence is as visible as contradiction
outcomes: reviewer sees each changed entity that no checkable claim covers | claim carries a flag for whether evidence could contradict it

description: An employer, customer contract, or regulator requires proof that a human reviewed AI-authored changes; teams treat accepted claims in a review-session as that sign-off and reviewers are pressed to bulk-accept claims to clear the queue
naive_change: Export the review-session event log listing, for every accepted claim, whether evidence corroborated, contradicted, or was absent at acceptance time, with reviewer identity and snapshot ids; never merge accepted and verified into one status
outcomes: reviewer exports each accepted claim with its evidence status at acceptance time | claim shows accepted and corroborated as separate statuses

description: Mirror pushes, backup clones, ref-scanning bots, and forges with allowlisted ref namespaces treat any diffcore-written ref as ordinary content, leaking pins to remotes, opening tickets, or rejecting pushes
naive_change: Never write refs into the reviewed project; pinned commits live in a bare repository inside the diffcore XDG store sharing objects via alternates
outcomes: reviewer pins a change-set snapshot without any ref appearing in the project | project shows no new refs after a review-session

description: Agent harnesses and security teams confine agent tools to sandboxes where only the project directory is writable, so an agent running the diffcore CLI or stdio MCP cannot write the XDG store and the only writable place is the project
naive_change: CLI and stdio entry points act as thin clients of the daemon running outside the sandbox; with no reachable daemon they run read-only in memory and report unsaved state; never fall back to a path inside the project
outcomes: agent runs diffcore in a project-only write sandbox and the project stays unchanged | reviewer is told when a review-session ran without saved state

description: Developers adopt jj, Sapling, git-branchless, or stacked-diff tools and agent loops amend and force-push dozens of times a day; the base and head the reviewer judged no longer exist anywhere the project can name
naive_change: Key a review-session to a lineage of snapshots rather than ref names; when a new head appears for the lineage (change-id trailers, patch-id similarity, or reviewer choice) create a successor snapshot and carry dispositions, claims, and queue items to anchors that re-resolve
outcomes: reviewer carries review-session dispositions to the successor change-set after a force-push | anchor reports exact, relocated, ambiguous, or missing for each carried claim

description: A change-set spanning security, data, and product code is reviewed by three humans on three machines with separate stores; nobody can see the others' dispositions or tell which concerns are settled
naive_change: Tag every review event with reviewer identity; export and import one review-session's events merged by event id, keeping each reviewer's dispositions separate and showing disagreements at the anchor
outcomes: reviewer imports another reviewer's events into a review-session without overwriting their own | reviewer sees where two reviewers disposed of the same anchor differently

description: Reviewers work in Codespaces, devcontainers, or ephemeral cloud workstations rebuilt on every start or reaped when idle; the review spans days but the home directory holding the store is fresh each morning and the browser runs on another machine
naive_change: Configurable store location, periodic and on-close export bundles imported on first start of a fresh environment, and serving over a forwarded origin advertised in the runtime file
outcomes: reviewer resumes a review-session in a rebuilt environment from an exported bundle | project registers in a new environment with its prior review-sessions attached

description: Endpoint security on managed laptops flags long-lived localhost listeners and unsigned background processes; policy forbids them, so the daemon, web surface, and MCP endpoint cannot stay up and the agent has nowhere to post claims
naive_change: Daemonless mode: stdio MCP holds state in-process against the store, the review-queue lives in the store for agents reading through stdio, and the reviewer view is a static export or short-lived foreground server
outcomes: agent answers a review-queue item through stdio MCP with no daemon running | reviewer reads a review-queue reply from an exported view without a listening port

description: Agent runs are short-lived: cloud tasks finish and their containers are deleted, threads are compacted until they forget the code, loops exit once tests pass; reviewer feedback arrives hours later with no live thread to answer it
naive_change: Make each review-queue item self-contained (anchor snapshot, original claim, reviewer comment, relevant evidence) with an export a fresh agent thread can take up; record which thread answered and whether it held the original context
outcomes: agent answers a review-queue item from a new thread using only the item contents | reviewer sees whether the replying thread wrote the code
